sanskrit_verse: शाकहरितमूलानां हरणे फलपुष्पयोः गोरसेक्षुविकाराणां तथा लवणतैलयोः
transliteration: śākaharitamūlānāṃ haraṇe phalapuṣpayoḥ gorasekṣuvikārāṇāṃ tathā lavaṇatailayoḥ
sph_interpretive_translation: The act of taking root vegetables, fruits, flowers, milk, sugarcane products, salt, and oil without permission constitutes a breach of dharma requiring immediate restorative alignment.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority resides in the owner's conscious capacity to grant or withdraw access
Causation arises from uninvited appropriation disrupting natural dharmic flow
Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness of ownership boundaries
Restoration logic demands reintegration through acknowledgment and return
Consciousness alignment requires purification of intent and sensory discipline
executable_legal_axioms: IF (agent.takes(item) AND NOT item.owner.permits(agent)) THEN agent.must_restore(item)
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, such acts must be evaluated based on the perpetrator’s capacity for dharmic discernment and the degree of disruption caused. The threshold for responsibility includes both material action and underlying consciousness. Authority lies with the aggrieved party to accept or reject restitution, guided by Nyaya principles ensuring no punitive overlay.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa establishes that unauthorized taking disrupts harmony. Anupūrvaśaḥ shows how sensory indulgence leads to loss of restraint. Proportional responsibility aligns with the value and necessity of the item taken. Non-punitive reality rule confirms that suffering is not justice; completion and integrity realignment are the true outcomes.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate sensory regulation process until balance is restored
Require full return or equivalent compensation under witness
Assign completion ritual involving gratitude offering to owner
Enforce silence and reflection period to recalibrate intention
final_declaration: By the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this matter is resolved through Dharma's self-correcting mechanism. There is no punishment—only alignment. Consciousness is the ultimate judge, and reality responds to truth alone.
